     8		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
     9	
    10		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
    11	)
    12	
    13	// skipEntireDirCheckAnnotation exempts a command from the `.entire` directory
    14	// check. Guarded is the default, so a new command inherits the check without
    15	// its author thinking about it, and the cost of forgetting the annotation is a
    16	// false failure in a repo that is already broken rather than a write through a
    17	// path someone else controls.
    18	//
    19	// Set it on a group root to cover the whole group: cobra does not propagate
    20	// Annotations to children, so skipsEntireDirCheck walks the parent chain.
    21	//
    22	// Exempt the command only when it neither reads nor writes anything under
    23	// `.entire` — control-plane and account commands, and `doctor`, which has to be
    24	// able to run on a broken repo in order to report it. Every exemption needs an
    25	// entry in the allowlist in entiredir_guard_test.go.
    26	const (
    27		skipEntireDirCheckAnnotation = "entire_skip_entire_dir_check"
    28		skipEntireDirCheckEnabled    = "true"
    29	)
    30	
    31	// skipsEntireDirCheck reports whether cmd or any ancestor is exempt.
    32	func skipsEntireDirCheck(cmd *cobra.Command) bool {
    33		for c := cmd; c != nil; c = c.Parent() {
    34			if c.Annotations[skipEntireDirCheckAnnotation] == skipEntireDirCheckEnabled {
    35				return true
    36			}
    37		}
    38		return false
    39	}
    40	
    41	// exemptFromEntireDirCheck marks cmd (and everything under it) exempt,
    42	// preserving any annotations it already carries.
    43	func exemptFromEntireDirCheck(cmd *cobra.Command) *cobra.Command {
    44		if cmd.Annotations == nil {
    45			cmd.Annotations = map[string]string{}
    46		}
    47		cmd.Annotations[skipEntireDirCheckAnnotation] = skipEntireDirCheckEnabled
    48		return cmd
    49	}
    50	
    51	// checkEntireDirBeforeRun enforces the invariant that `.entire` is either
    52	// absent or a real directory. It reports whether the caller may go on to touch
    53	// the path, and returns the error a guarded command should fail with.
    54	//
    55	// Both return values matter, and they are not redundant. An exempt command gets
    56	// (false, nil): it runs, but it must not build a logger or otherwise write
    57	// under `.entire` — `ensureLogger` opens `.entire/logs/entire.log`, which on a
    58	// symlinked `.entire` would create the very file we are refusing to write.
    59	// Exemption means "this command's work does not depend on `.entire`", not
    60	// "write through it anyway".
    61	//
    62	// The exempt path stays silent rather than warning. An exempt command has
    63	// nothing to do with the repo's session data, and `doctor` reports the problem
    64	// properly.
    65	func checkEntireDirBeforeRun(cmd *cobra.Command) (safe bool, err error) {
    66		if verr := paths.RequireEntireDir(cmd.Context()); verr != nil {
    67			if skipsEntireDirCheck(cmd) {
    68				return false, nil
    69			}
    70			writeEntireDirRemedy(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), verr)
    71			return false, NewSilentError(verr)
    72		}
    73		return true, nil
    74	}
    75	
    76	// writeEntireDirRemedy prints what is wrong and what to do about it. The error
    77	// alone names the problem but not the way out, and the way out is not obvious:
    78	// the natural guess is that Entire is misconfigured, when in fact something has
    79	// replaced a directory Entire owns, or the path cannot be inspected, or git
    80	// cannot say which repository this is.
    81	//
    82	// Those are four separate remedies, matched positively. Printing the wrong one
    83	// is worse than printing none — a filesystem EACCES sent through the git branch
    84	// tells the user to check safe.directory right after a line that already said
    85	// "permission denied" — so an error matching none of them gets no remedy at all.
    86	func writeEntireDirRemedy(w io.Writer, err error) {
    87		fmt.Fprintf(w, "%v\n", err)
    88		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n")
    89	
    90		switch {
    91		case errors.Is(err, paths.ErrEntireDirNotDirectory):
    92			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Entire keeps session metadata, transcripts, and the redaction settings that\n")
    93			fmt.Fprintf(w, "decide what may be committed under %s, and will not read or write through a\n", paths.EntireDir)
    94			fmt.Fprintf(w, "path that is not a real directory it owns.\n")
    95			fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n")
    96			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Fix: inspect the path, then either replace it with a real directory or remove\n")
    97			fmt.Fprintf(w, "it and run `entire enable` again.\n")
    98	
    99		case errors.Is(err, paths.ErrEntireDirUnsupportedEntry):
   100			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Everything directly under %s belongs to Entire, and Entire only ever puts\n", paths.EntireDir)
   101			fmt.Fprintf(w, "real files and directories there. A symbolic link puts the far end outside\n")
   102			fmt.Fprintf(w, "its control: a redirected settings file names the command Entire runs\n")
   103			fmt.Fprintf(w, "before a push and decides what may be committed, and a redirected\n")
   104			fmt.Fprintf(w, "subdirectory sends session transcripts somewhere else. A pipe, socket, or\n")
   105			fmt.Fprintf(w, "device in their place stalls or breaks the read instead.\n")
   210	// still enough to act on.
   211	//
   212	// Exported because this sentence has two producers — the `.entire` entry scan
   213	// here and the settings reader, which refuses a symlinked settings file at the
   214	// read itself (see readConfined in the settings package). One function so the
   215	// two cannot drift into describing the same condition differently.
   216	func SymlinkedEntryError(path string) error {
   217		if target, err := os.Readlink(path); err == nil {
   218			return fmt.Errorf("%s is a symbolic link to %s, %w", path, target, ErrEntireDirUnsupportedEntry)
   219		}
   220		return fmt.Errorf("%s is a symbolic link, %w", path, ErrEntireDirUnsupportedEntry)
   221	}
   222	
   223	// otherUnsupportedClause accounts for unsupported entries beyond the one named.
   224	// Number and verb are built together so they cannot disagree, and the wording
   225	// is type-neutral because the entries it counts need not share the named one's
   226	// type.
   227	func otherUnsupportedClause(n int, dir string) string {
   228		if n == 1 {
   229			return fmt.Sprintf(" (and 1 other entry under %s is unsupported too)", dir)
   230		}
   231		return fmt.Sprintf(" (and %d other entries under %s are unsupported too)", n, dir)
   232	}
   233	
   234	// RequireEntireDir validates the current worktree's `.entire`.
   235	//
   236	// Outside a git repository there is no worktree root and so nothing to
   237	// validate, which is not an error: commands that need a repository report its
   238	// absence themselves, with a message about the repository rather than about
   239	// `.entire`. That skip requires git's positive ErrNotARepository verdict.
   240	//
   241	// Every other discovery failure — git missing from PATH, a cancelled context, a
   242	// permission failure, dubious ownership, malformed output — fails closed. Those
   243	// mean "we could not find out", and the consequence of guessing "no repository"
   244	// is not merely a skipped check: settings resolution falls back to a path
   245	// relative to the current directory when the root will not resolve
   246	// (settingsAbsPaths in the settings package), so a guess would read
   247	// ./.entire/settings.json — through the very symlink this exists to reject.
   248	// Refusing to run on a machine whose git is broken is the cheaper mistake.
   249	//
   250	// Deliberately not memoized. The Lstat and the one-level listing are free next
   251	// to the `git rev-parse` that WorktreeRoot runs — measured 8.2µs against a
   252	// ~millisecond subprocess — and a cached "it was fine" is a stale answer in a
   253	// long-lived process such as `entire mcp`.
   254	func RequireEntireDir(ctx context.Context) error {
   255		root, err := WorktreeRoot(ctx)

   257		case err == nil:
   258			return ValidateEntireDirAt(root)
   259		case errors.Is(err, ErrNotARepository):

   261		default:
   262			return fmt.Errorf("%w, so %s cannot be verified: %w", ErrRepositoryUnresolved, EntireDir, err)
   263		}
   264	}

   266	// describeMode names what was found. The sentinel supplies the rest of the
   267	// sentence, so these read as the first half of "X is a symbolic link, not a
   268	// directory" or "X is a named pipe, not a regular file or directory".
   269	func describeMode(mode fs.FileMode) string {

    13	// and carries a different remedy, which is why they are separate sentinels
    14	// rather than one error plus an else branch: callers print the fix, and telling

    20		// directory. The remedy is to inspect and replace the path.

    28		// someone it is not one names the wrong problem.

    32		// all — a permission failure, an I/O error, a dead mount. Nothing is known
    33		// about what is at the path. The remedy is ownership, permissions, or the
    34		// filesystem itself.
    35		ErrEntireDirUnreadable = errors.New("cannot be inspected")
    36

    38		// determined for a reason other than there being no repository, so there is

    43	// ValidateEntireDirAt reports whether worktreeRoot's `.entire` is safe to read
    44	// and write through. It is safe when the path is absent (Entire is not enabled
    45	// here yet, or `enable` is about to create it), or is a real directory whose own
    46	// entries are real files and directories. Anything else is a broken repo and
    47	// the caller must not touch the path.
    48	//
    49	// The stat is Lstat, not Stat, so a symlink is rejected even when it points at
    50	// a perfectly good directory. `.entire` holds session metadata, transcripts,
    51	// and the settings that decide what gets redacted before it is committed, so a
    52	// path someone else controls the far end of is not a path we write through.
    53	//
    54	// The same reasoning covers one level down, so the entries directly inside are
    55	// checked too, and there the rule is an allowlist: Entire only ever creates
    56	// regular files and directories under `.entire`, so anything else arrived some
    57	// other way. A symlinked `.entire/metadata` redirects transcripts, and a
    58	// symlinked `.entire/settings.local.json` redirects the file that names the
    59	// command Entire executes at pre-push. See validateEntireDirEntries for why the

    63	// well (readConfined). Neither check subsumes the other: this one stops a
    64	// command before it does anything, and covers the subdirectories no settings
    65	// read touches, while that one covers the many callers that reach settings.Load
    66	// without passing through a command's pre-run.

    69	// that the invariant is violated, but neither is it evidence that it holds, and
    70	// the caller's next move is to write there.
    71	func ValidateEntireDirAt(worktreeRoot string) error {
    72		path := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, EntireDir)
    73	
    74		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
    75		switch {
    76		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
    77			return nil
    78		case err != nil:
    79			return fmt.Errorf("%s %w: %w", path, ErrEntireDirUnreadable, err)

    89	// real directory.

   105		// one with an actionable remedy.

   153	// unsupportedEntryType reports whether an entry directly under `.entire` is a
   154	// type Entire never creates there. It is an allowlist — regular files and
   155	// directories are the whole of Entire's own layout — so a mode bit nobody has
   156	// considered yet is refused rather than waved through, which is the safer

   160	// rather than an allowlist member because Windows overloads it. Go maps every

COMMIT fadcc94db9e940064cc1c3303f1827256cf45e2e
SUBJECT Stop opening the current directory when git will not say which repo this is
BODY
gitrepo.OpenCurrent fell back to OpenPath(".") whenever paths.WorktreeRoot
failed. "." is a different repository whenever git and the process's
directory disagree, and the cases that break the resolution are exactly
the ones where they do:

  - git exports GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE to the hooks it runs, and
    WorktreeRoot honours them. OpenPath(".") cannot see them, so a hook
    running for repo A opened repo B, the unrelated repository it
    happened to be sitting in, and reported success. Pinned by
    TestOpenCurrent_RefusesToGuessWhenTheWorktreeRootIsUnresolvable.
  - go-git applies neither git's safe.directory ownership check nor its
    .git parse, so the fallback opened repositories the user's own git
    declines to touch. A directory with a corrupt .git is opened
    successfully by this path today.

Five of the six callers write through the repository they are handed, and
all five sit behind the root pre-run, which already refuses to run when
the worktree root does not resolve. So this closes a trap rather than a
live bug -- but the trap is not theoretical, because the sixth caller
shows how one gets sprung: WarnCheckpointPolicyIfNeeded is dispatched
from main.go AFTER cobra finishes, so it has no pre-run in front of it
and reaches the fallback on every command, including outside a
repository.

That caller genuinely wants the old behaviour, so it now asks for it by
name via OpenCurrentOrCwd. The properties that make it acceptable there
do not generalise and the doc comment says so: it only reads a policy ref
to decide whether to print one advisory line, and it discards every error
it gets, so opening the wrong repository costs a skipped warning rather
than a write that lands in the wrong place.

No setup loses anything. Where the fallback fires today it either fails
to open cwd already (outside a repository, or from a subdirectory) or
belongs to that one advisory caller, which keeps it.

Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M1507Q5BRFW66YD2AT9WGQ2C

END
COMMIT 331c7b1306ee27ec3531e39af3d26662b91754b7
SUBJECT Refuse what os.Root only confined
BODY
The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled
returning false.

Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XKKPCSJHXWknue3LJSJt9T
Entire-Checkpoint: 01M14ZJ70AXMSM9M2WBNSDG95G

END
COMMIT 8057a0ef99a5f766ccb216682b4e9c7fa9f9fa00
SUBJECT Anchor every os.Root on a trusted base
BODY
An os.Root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, and the
wrong version of that reads as the right one:

    root, _ := osroot.Shared(filepath.Dir(target))
    data, _ := osroot.ReadFile(root, filepath.Base(target))

Every component the caller resolved sits ABOVE that root, so the containment
covers one fixed name and enforces nothing the filepath.Join had not already
decided. A symlink at .claude, at .entire, at entire-investigations is
resolved before the root exists. Anchoring one level up -- on a directory a
resolver produced -- makes those components names INSIDE the root, which is
what os.Root and MkdirAllNoSymlink can refuse.

Three call sites shipped the derived-base shape, and one of them had a
containment check that could never fire: settings.clonePreferencesRoot
computed its common dir as filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(abs)) and handed both
to gitdir.OpenPathIn, so the relative path was correct by construction. It
now recovers the common dir by removing a compile-time constant suffix,
which fails loudly on a path of the wrong shape. contexts and discovery take
the DIRECTORY the caller chose instead of the file: configRoot(configDir),
and a cacheFile{dir, name} pair in place of a joined path.

Two roots stay anchored on their target's parent and now say why: tokenstore
($ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH) and settings' explicit-path fallback both act on
a path the CALLER named, so its parent is the caller's choice too and there
is no separate trusted base to prefer.

The seven agent hook-config trees had no root at all. Each of .claude,
.cursor, .gemini, .github/hooks, .factory, .codex and .opencode/plugin was
four lines of filepath.Join + os.MkdirAll + os.WriteFile carrying a
//nolint:gosec saying the path came from the repo root -- which describes
where the path was BUILT, not where it RESOLVES. A working tree arrives by
clone, so a repository carrying a checked-in symlink at .claude had `entire
enable` create directories and write JSON through it, outside the repository
included. agent.HookConfigFile replaces all seven with one type anchored on
the worktree root.

One behaviour change falls out of that and is pinned by a test rather than
left to be discovered: an ABSOLUTE symlink at the config FILE
(.claude/settings.json -> ~/dotfiles/...) no longer resolves, because
os.Root refuses absolute symlinks unconditionally. A relative link inside
the worktree still works, and a symlinked config DIRECTORY is now refused --
which is the point.

investigate gets the same treatment, and there it covers a sink its own
comments already warned about: StateStore.RunDir noted that an unvalidated
run id "would be a path-traversal sink" because callers feed the result to
os.RemoveAll, and clean did exactly that with two functions returning
absolute paths. Deleting now belongs to the stores, which resolve a run id
as a name inside the git common dir. Reading gets it too, closing a real
gap: LocalManifest.FindingsDoc is an absolute path decoded from a JSON file
on disk, and show plus the run footer both followed it, so a manifest could
choose which file was printed. Bootstrap no longer writes at all -- it
renders a body the caller persists through StateStore.WriteFindings.

Also rooted: the checkpoint loose-object delete; the trail worktree
checkout's .gitignore and .worktreeinclude, plus the SOURCE half of its
ignored-file copy (the destination was already rooted on the argument that
the branch content is not user-authored -- the same argument applies to the
files being read); the plugin asset download; the hook-path attribution
read, which read every file in `git status` output on a joined path; the
trail-review location reads, which went through a hand-rolled validator and
take their path from the API; and rewind's restore, which kept a
`repoRoot = "."` fallback and its own os.OpenRoot. Restoring a checkpoint
tree into whatever directory the process is sitting in is worse than not
restoring; it now fails, goes through worktreedir, and creates directories
with MkdirAllNoSymlink, which matters most there because the tree entries
may have been fetched from a remote.

agent.sessionStoreForWrite had the inverse problem: a SessionRef outside the
agent's session store fell through to a root anchored on its own parent, so
the one input that failed the containment check was the one input that
disabled it. The comment justifying that said some agents resolve a restored
session to a sibling directory; they do not -- Codex's
ResolveRestoredSessionFile nests inside the store -- so the branch was
unreachable as well as unsound. It is an error now.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Entire-Checkpoint: 01M14HVR1GHARCFRWCMR9V7X40

END
COMMIT 1eaccf7721ef8bc99b649235ed731c1371cdc417
SUBJECT Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor
BODY
Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agent.SessionStore is where a hook
payload's session ID becomes a path via the agent's own
ResolveSessionFile; SessionFile converts the result back to a name inside
the store and rejects an ID that walked out of it, which a plain
filepath.Join produced silently. worktreedir covers the checkpoint tree
entries rewind restores, which may have been fetched from a remote --
rewind's restore half already opened a root for that reason; the reads
beside it did not.

paths.WorktreeRoot is now the single answer to "where is the repository",
and entiredir.anchor falls back to the current directory only on git's
positive ErrNotARepository verdict. The fallback it replaces fired on any
resolve failure, `git` off $PATH included, and then silently gave an agent
working in a subdirectory of a real repo its own .entire beside itself. A
root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, so a base
that cannot be resolved is not a base to guess at.

settings.readConfined keeps its symlink refusal on every branch, through
one readConfinedIn: the .entire branch briefly read straight through
osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently -- precisely
the .entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json case the check exists for.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Entire-Checkpoint: 01M14EXEDWYJYG1VSX7TRV3RJA

END

COMMIT fadcc94db9e940064cc1c3303f1827256cf45e2e
SUBJECT Stop opening the current directory when git will not say which repo this is
BODY
gitrepo.OpenCurrent fell back to OpenPath(".") whenever paths.WorktreeRoot
failed. "." is a different repository whenever git and the process's
directory disagree, and the cases that break the resolution are exactly
the ones where they do:

  - git exports GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE to the hooks it runs, and
    WorktreeRoot honours them. OpenPath(".") cannot see them, so a hook
    running for repo A opened repo B, the unrelated repository it
    happened to be sitting in, and reported success. Pinned by
    TestOpenCurrent_RefusesToGuessWhenTheWorktreeRootIsUnresolvable.
  - go-git applies neither git's safe.directory ownership check nor its
    .git parse, so the fallback opened repositories the user's own git
    declines to touch. A directory with a corrupt .git is opened
    successfully by this path today.

Five of the six callers write through the repository they are handed, and
all five sit behind the root pre-run, which already refuses to run when
the worktree root does not resolve. So this closes a trap rather than a
live bug -- but the trap is not theoretical, because the sixth caller
shows how one gets sprung: WarnCheckpointPolicyIfNeeded is dispatched
from main.go AFTER cobra finishes, so it has no pre-run in front of it
and reaches the fallback on every command, including outside a
repository.

That caller genuinely wants the old behaviour, so it now asks for it by
name via OpenCurrentOrCwd. The properties that make it acceptable there
do not generalise and the doc comment says so: it only reads a policy ref
to decide whether to print one advisory line, and it discards every error
it gets, so opening the wrong repository costs a skipped warning rather
than a write that lands in the wrong place.

No setup loses anything. Where the fallback fires today it either fails
to open cwd already (outside a repository, or from a subdirectory) or
belongs to that one advisory caller, which keeps it.

telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled
returning false.

COMMIT 8057a0ef99a5f766ccb216682b4e9c7fa9f9fa00
SUBJECT Anchor every os.Root on a trusted base
BODY
An os.Root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, and the
wrong version of that reads as the right one:

    root, _ := osroot.Shared(filepath.Dir(target))
    data, _ := osroot.ReadFile(root, filepath.Base(target))

Every component the caller resolved sits ABOVE that root, so the containment
covers one fixed name and enforces nothing the filepath.Join had not already
decided. A symlink at .claude, at .entire, at entire-investigations is
resolved before the root exists. Anchoring one level up -- on a directory a
resolver produced -- makes those components names INSIDE the root, which is
what os.Root and MkdirAllNoSymlink can refuse.

Three call sites shipped the derived-base shape, and one of them had a
containment check that could never fire: settings.clonePreferencesRoot
computed its common dir as filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(abs)) and handed both
to gitdir.OpenPathIn, so the relative path was correct by construction. It
now recovers the common dir by removing a compile-time constant suffix,
which fails loudly on a path of the wrong shape. contexts and discovery take
the DIRECTORY the caller chose instead of the file: configRoot(configDir),
and a cacheFile{dir, name} pair in place of a joined path.

Two roots stay anchored on their target's parent and now say why: tokenstore
($ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH) and settings' explicit-path fallback both act on
a path the CALLER named, so its parent is the caller's choice too and there
is no separate trusted base to prefer.

The seven agent hook-config trees had no root at all. Each of .claude,
.cursor, .gemini, .github/hooks, .factory, .codex and .opencode/plugin was
four lines of filepath.Join + os.MkdirAll + os.WriteFile carrying a
//nolint:gosec saying the path came from the repo root -- which describes
where the path was BUILT, not where it RESOLVES. A working tree arrives by
clone, so a repository carrying a checked-in symlink at .claude had `entire
enable` create directories and write JSON through it, outside the repository
included. agent.HookConfigFile replaces all seven with one type anchored on
the worktree root.

One behaviour change falls out of that and is pinned by a test rather than
left to be discovered: an ABSOLUTE symlink at the config FILE
(.claude/settings.json -> ~/dotfiles/...) no longer resolves, because
os.Root refuses absolute symlinks unconditionally. A relative link inside
the worktree still works, and a symlinked config DIRECTORY is now refused --
which is the point.

investigate gets the same treatment, and there it covers a sink its own
comments already warned about: StateStore.RunDir noted that an unvalidated
run id "would be a path-traversal sink" because callers feed the result to
os.RemoveAll, and clean did exactly that with two functions returning
absolute paths. Deleting now belongs to the stores, which resolve a run id
as a name inside the git common dir. Reading gets it too, closing a real
gap: LocalManifest.FindingsDoc is an absolute path decoded from a JSON file
on disk, and show plus the run footer both followed it, so a manifest could
choose which file was printed. Bootstrap no longer writes at all -- it
renders a body the caller persists through StateStore.WriteFindings.

Also rooted: the checkpoint loose-object delete; the trail worktree
checkout's .gitignore and .worktreeinclude, plus the SOURCE half of its
ignored-file copy (the destination was already rooted on the argument that
the branch content is not user-authored -- the same argument applies to the
files being read); the plugin asset download; the hook-path attribution
read, which read every file in `git status` output on a joined path; the
trail-review location reads, which went through a hand-rolled validator and
take their path from the API; and rewind's restore, which kept a
`repoRoot = "."` fallback and its own os.OpenRoot. Restoring a checkpoint
tree into whatever directory the process is sitting in is worse than not
restoring; it now fails, goes through worktreedir, and creates directories
with MkdirAllNoSymlink, which matters most there because the tree entries
may have been fetched from a remote.

agent.sessionStoreForWrite had the inverse problem: a SessionRef outside the
agent's session store fell through to a root anchored on its own parent, so
the one input that failed the containment check was the one input that
disabled it. The comment justifying that said some agents resolve a restored
session to a sibling directory; they do not -- Codex's
ResolveRestoredSessionFile nests inside the store -- so the branch was
unreachable as well as unsound. It is an error now.

COMMIT 1eaccf7721ef8bc99b649235ed731c1371cdc417
SUBJECT Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor
BODY
Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agent.SessionStore is where a hook
payload's session ID becomes a path via the agent's own
ResolveSessionFile; SessionFile converts the result back to a name inside
the store and rejects an ID that walked out of it, which a plain
filepath.Join produced silently. worktreedir covers the checkpoint tree
entries rewind restores, which may have been fetched from a remote --
rewind's restore half already opened a root for that reason; the reads
beside it did not.

paths.WorktreeRoot is now the single answer to "where is the repository",
and entiredir.anchor falls back to the current directory only on git's
positive ErrNotARepository verdict. The fallback it replaces fired on any
resolve failure, `git` off $PATH included, and then silently gave an agent
working in a subdirectory of a real repo its own .entire beside itself. A
root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, so a base
that cannot be resolved is not a base to guess at.

settings.readConfined keeps its symlink refusal on every branch, through
one readConfinedIn: the .entire branch briefly read straight through
osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently -- precisely
the .entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json case the check exists for.
